name: New Jersey
headline_status: Recreational and medical cannabis are legal for adults 21+.
summary: New Jersey voters approved legalization in November 2020, Gov. Phil Murphy signed the implementing laws on February 22, 2021, and licensed adult-use sales began in April 2022. Adults may possess up to 6 ounces and buy up to 1 ounce per transaction, but home growing remains illegal. The medical program dates to 2010, and bills to allow home cultivation are under consideration.

adult_use_since.value: Voters approved legalization in November 2020; Gov. Murphy signed the implementing laws February 22, 2021.

possession_limit.value: Adults may possess up to 6 ounces; purchases are capped at 1 ounce of flower (or 4 g concentrate, or 1,000 mg of edibles) per transaction.

purchase_age.value: 21 and older, for residents and visitors alike.

public_use.value: Allowed in private spaces (unless a landlord forbids it), wherever cigarette smoking is allowed, and in licensed consumption areas.

retail_sales.value: Licensed adult-use sales began in April 2022.

taxes.value: 6.625% sales tax plus a social equity excise fee of one-third of one percent.

timeline.event: Voters approve a legalization referendum with more than two-thirds support.
Gov. Murphy signs the legalization and decriminalization laws.

pending.item: S2564 would allow adults to grow cannabis at home.
A1674/S1758 would let medical patients grow up to 4 mature and 4 immature plants.

faq.q: Is weed legal in New Jersey?
faq.a: Yes. Adults 21 and older can buy and possess cannabis, and patients can use it under the medical program.

faq.q: How much weed can you buy in New Jersey?
faq.a: Up to 1 ounce of flower per transaction, or equivalent amounts of concentrate or edibles; adults may possess up to 6 ounces.

faq.q: Can you grow weed in New Jersey?
faq.a: No. Home cultivation is still illegal, though bills to allow it have been introduced.

faq.q: Can tourists buy weed in New Jersey?
faq.a: Yes. Anyone 21 or older with a valid government ID can buy, but taking cannabis across state lines is illegal.

sources.name: NJ Cannabis Regulatory Commission, Adult Personal Use
